title: RNA Isolation from Plant Tissue Using TRIzol Extraction
author: Ambion
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.4u6gwze
materials: Clean all surfaces and equipment with 20 % bleach, 95 % ethanol, and RNase Zap, and place supplies in hood.
Prepare aliquots of the following solutions into 50mL Falcon tubes: 75 % ethanol, 100 % chloroform, 100 % isopropanol.
Keep on liquid nitrogen, until TRIzol is added.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare labeled microcentrifuge tubes containing 5 zirconia beads.

steps.title: Prepare Frozen Tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer 60 mg to 100 mg of frozen plant tissue from 50 ml Falcon tubes into the microcentrifuge tubes using forceps or a spatula. For aquatic plants, use 2x the weight.

substeps.instruction: Fill two small coolers with liquid N2 (one for microcentrifuge tubes, one for Falcon tubes).
Verify the weight of each sample and add more if necessary.
Ensure beads are moving freely within the tube.

steps.title: Pulverize Frozen Tissue
steps.instruction: Pulverize the tissue using an automatic shaker while keeping samples frozen in liquid N2.

substeps.instruction: Place samples in a black shaker block sitting in a bath of liquid N2.
Quickly transfer the block into the automatic shaker to prevent thawing.
Shake for 00:02:00.
If needed, place the block back into the liquid nitrogen cooler to shake for another 00:02:00.

steps.title: Lysis and Homogenization
steps.instruction: Lyse the tissue using TRIzol solution and optional Sarkosyl.

substeps.instruction: Tap the tube on the bench to move leaf tissue from the lid into the tube.
Add 1 mL of TRIzol solution (optionally add 50 µL to 100 µL of 20% Sarkosyl).
Vortex immediately (top and bottom of tube) until all tissue is hydrated; this may take up to 00:02:00.
Place tubes on ice sequentially until all 24 tubes are finished.
Incubate the batch at room temperature for 00:05:00.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Separate the aqueous phase from the cellular debris.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge for 00:10:00 at 4 °C.
Pipette the aqueous solution (approximately 800 µL to 900 µL) into a new 1.7 ml tube, avoiding the viscous Sarkosyl layer at the interface if used.

steps.title: RNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the nucleic acids using isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of isopropanol to the aqueous solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 00:10:00.
Centrifuge for 00:15:00 at 4 °C.
Pour off the supernatant as waste.

steps.title: Ethanol Wash
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet to remove salts and contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Add 1000 mL of 75% ethanol to the tube with the pellet.
Centrifuge for 00:05:00 at 4 °C.
Pour off ethanol into a beaker and tap the tube to remove as much ethanol as possible.
Centrifuge the 'empty' tube for 00:02:00 at 4 °C.
Use a pipette to remove any remaining excess ethanol from the bottom; the final pellet should be clear (repeat wash if pellet is white).

steps.title: RNA Re-dissolution
steps.instruction: Dry and dissolve the RNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Let the pellet dry at room temperature for 00:02:00 (maximum 00:10:00).
Re-dissolve in 50 µL of RNase-free water.
If the pellet does not dissolve immediately, incubate at 55 °C for 00:10:00 in a water bath (do not exceed 10 mins or increase temperature), or store at 4 °C overnight.
Vortex gently and transfer to a new tube.

steps.title: Quantification and Dilution
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration using a NanoDrop.

substeps.instruction: Check concentration; dilute samples to less than 200 ng/μl if they exceed 2000-3000 ng/μl before proceeding to DNase steps.

steps.title: DNA Removal
steps.instruction: Remove genomic DNA using the Turbo DNA-free kit.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.1 volume of 10X Turbo DNase buffer (typically 5 µL) and 1 µL of Turbo DNase to the RNA; mix gently.
Incubate at 37 °C for 00:30:00 while shaking on an orbiter inside an incubation oven.
Add resuspended DNase Inactivation Reagent (typically 0.1 volume; 5 µL) and mix well via brief vortexing.
Incubate at room temperature for 00:02:00, vortexing occasionally.
Centrifuge for 00:01:30 at 4 °C.

steps.title: Final Quality Control
steps.instruction: Perform final NanoDrop measurement to verify purity and concentration.

substeps.instruction: Verify that the OD 260/280 ratio is between 1.8 and 2.2 (not less than 1.6).

steps.title: Optional Chloroform Purification
steps.instruction: Perform additional purification if the sample appears contaminated or Sarkosyl was used.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL of 100% chloroform to each tube.
Vortex for 00:00:10 – 00:00:15 until the solution is milky.
Incubate at room temperature for 00:10:00.
Centrifuge for 00:15:00 at 4 °C without disturbing the layers.
Remove the clear upper aqueous layer (500 µL to 700 µL) and transfer to a new 1.7 ml tube.
